questions.scenario: A diagram is printed with the first part. It shows: Two drawings of springs hanging from a wooden support, each with a mass at the bottom. In (a), two springs are joined end to end in a single line (in series) and hang from the support, with a mass attached to the lower end. In (b), two springs hang side by side (in parallel) from the support, and a single rod across their lower ends holds one mass.
questions.question: Explain the difference in the extension of the springs in the series and parallel arrangements when the same mass is attached.
marking_criteria: Explain extension in series arrangement
Explain extension in parallel arrangement
Compare the two extensions
hints: Stay focused on this: Explain the difference in the extension of the springs in the series and parallel arrangements when the same mass is attached — develop the idea fully rather than listing short points. Make sure you also cover: Compare the two.
questions.model_answer: In the series arrangement, the same force stretches both springs, so the total extension is the sum of the extensions of each spring. In the parallel arrangement, the force is shared between the springs, so each spring extends less than in the series arrangement. Therefore, the total extension in the parallel arrangement is less than in the series arrangement.
questions.explanation: In a series arrangement, the total extension is the sum of the extensions of each spring because they are connected end to end. In a parallel arrangement, the force is shared between the springs, so each spring extends less, leading to a smaller total extension.

questions.scenario: A cylindrical tank with a flat base is filled with water to a height of 1.5 m. The base area of the tank is 0.5 m².
questions.question: Calculate the pressure at the bottom of the tank due to the water column.
marking_criteria: Correct use of the formula for pressure (P = ρgh)
Substitution of the given values into the formula
Correct calculation and unit
hints: Recall the formula for pressure in a fluid at rest: P = ρgh, where ρ is the density of the fluid, g is the acceleration due to gravity, and h is the height of the fluid column.
questions.model_answer: Pressure (P) = Density (ρ) x Gravity (g) x Height (h) = 1000 kg/m³ x 9.8 m/s² x 1.5 m = 14700 Pa
questions.explanation: Use the formula for pressure in a fluid to calculate the pressure at the bottom of the tank due to the water column.

questions.scenario: A cylindrical tank with a flat base is filled with water to a height of 1.5 m. The base area of the tank is 0.5 m².
questions.question: Determine the total force exerted by the water on the base of the tank.

questions.scenario: A balloon is filled with helium to a volume of 2.0 m³ at a pressure of 1.0 x 10¹ Pa. The balloon is then taken to a higher altitude where the atmospheric pressure decreases to 0.5 x 10¹ Pa.
questions.question: Calculate the new volume of the balloon at the higher altitude, assuming the temperature remains constant.

questions.model_answer: Using Boyle's Law: P1V1 = P2V2, 1.0 x 10¹ Pa x 2.0 m³ = 0.5 x 10¹ Pa x V2, V2 = 4.0 m³
